legislation.cert_required: UL or equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory
legislation.notes: PL 2026 c.644, approved 6 April 2026, enacts 35-A MRSA 3475. An 'eligible system' is a plug-in photovoltaic or plug-in battery system with an EXPORT CAPACITY of 1,200 watts or less, listed or certified to UL 3700 or a comparable standard, using inverters configured to shut off within 0.2 seconds if power is disrupted. Subsection 3 sets the tiers in COMBINED INVERTER OUTPUT measured in alternating current: up to 420 W per service address with no further condition; above 420 W and up to 1,200 W each system must be installed by an electrician licensed in the State and use a dedicated circuit with a single outlet. Subsection 5: the customer must notify the utility on a form prescribed by the Commission within 30 days of installation; the utility may not deny a compliant installation. Subsection 4: an eligible system MAY NOT be used for net energy billing under 3209-A or 3209-B. Subsection 8: a customer installing on a structure they do not own must not compromise its integrity or violate state or local building, fire or zoning codes.

watt_tiers.effect: Above 420 W: must be installed by an electrician licensed in Maine, on a dedicated circuit with a single outlet, with notification to the utility within 30 days of installation. No interconnection application, agreement, study, fee or extra equipment. Not eligible for net energy billing.

watt_tiers.basis: combined inverter output, measured in alternating current
watt_tiers.effect: May be installed and operated by the customer with no electrician requirement, no dedicated-circuit requirement and no notification.
